task: Revise the collection semantics oracle to match approved language decisions.
observation: The historical ORACLE-05 fixture required Map.get to return option[V], and its MATCH_REQUIRES_ENUM result was reported as a compiler defect. The revised directive instead specifies borrowed V. A direct one-argument Map.get probe against the task baseline now reports that builtin get expects two arguments, so the old fixture was not a valid test of the approved contract and current compiler conformance remains unresolved.
impact: Oracle expectations need explicit spec ownership and must test operations directly; a diagnostic mismatch can be caused by a stale oracle assumption. The revised fixture now directly exercises the approved Map.get form.
evidence: build/compiler/moss-dev check --json tests/phase28/oracle/fixtures/oracle_05_map_get_borrowed.moss -> TYPE_MISMATCH: builtin get(key, default) expects 2 arguments, got 1

resolution.summary: The oracle expectation is corrected in the draft; implementing and validating the approved one-argument Map.get contract is outside this compiler-source-excluded task.

task: Harden rejection, panic and clone-provenance validation for the L7 resubmission.
observation: The original harness treated any nonzero exit as an expected panic and accepted rejection diagnostics by substring. The structured CLI response exposes source file, line, severity, code and message, so the revised harness can reject unrelated compilation errors and unrelated runtime crashes. The full oracle also confirms 298 generated Rust .clone() occurrences without sidecars; these remain unverified rather than proven hidden Moss-value clones.
impact: Specification-based expectations require structured evidence tied to the exact fixture operation. Missing clone provenance must be reported as an independent infrastructure gate so it does not blur semantic conformance results.
evidence: tmp/phase28_r7_005_revised/run.log (56 fixtures; 34 semantic failures; 19 provenance-blocked; 298 unverified occurrences)

resolution.summary: The revised draft parses structured diagnostics, validates panic evidence, self-tests adversarial cases, separates semantic/provenance outcomes and documents scanner limits. L7 approval, independent harness review and compiler-emitted provenance are still pending.

task: Resolve final L7 findings on expectation and clone-provenance correctness.
observation: A fixture's observable mutation expected line and value can contradict the per-engine stdout even when the table parses and fixture executes. ORACLE-07 pointed at line 9 instead of the final value on line 11, and ORACLE-49 expected 7 where the surviving source element is 8. The copy scanner also skipped nested calls because it advanced beyond the outer span.
impact: Data validation now cross-checks every mutation assertion against all three expected engine outputs before launching the compiler. Nested copy calls are independently identified. Runtime origin labels cannot authorize clones unless they match a digest-pinned, independently reviewed callsite registry; the draft registry is empty.

resolution.summary: Final corrections are implemented and the draft run completed; L7 approval is still required before freezing.
